invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: CPH number: three labelled boxes as drawn, no cursor jump, and the whole number kept when typed or pasted in one go, in animals
increments.detail: The designers asked for the cursor to jump to the next CPH box when one is full (S37). Sam ruled on 20 October: no cursor jump. Moving focus while someone types fails WCAG 3.2.2 unless users are told first, and GOV.UK forms do not do it. The real problem the designers saw is that typing the 9 digits straight through keeps only '12': each box has a maxlength of 2, 3 or 4, so the browser drops every keystroke after County is full. This row keeps the prototype's three boxes, each with a visible label and styled as drawn, and drops the maxlength cut-off so nothing typed or pasted is lost. When County holds the whole number and Parish and Holding are empty, the server splits it into the three parts on save. That works without JavaScript and needs no new client script. The prototype's own digit filter and paste spreading stay in waiting-on-design inc-093. openspec: live-animals/journey-pages cph-number: no automatic focus moves; the whole number typed into County is kept and split on save.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the CPH number page on a live-animals notification, when it shows, then the 'CPH number' question has three boxes in one row, each with a visible label ('County', 'Parish', 'Holding number', Welsh as today), 2, 3 and 4 characters wide, laid out and styled as the prototype draws them. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/cph-number.html p9-011; screens/prototype/S37--all-typed-continuously.png)

Given the CPH number page, with JavaScript on or off, when the trader fills a box, then focus stays in that box: nothing moves focus to the next box, and Backspace in an empty box does not move focus back. (Sam, 20 Oct: no cursor jump; c-006; req-713 out of scope)

Given the CPH number page with JavaScript off, when the trader types '123456789' straight through into County, then County shows all nine digits; no box cuts typing short. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; screens/main/S37--whole-number-typed.png shows only '12' kept today)

Given County holds '123456789', '12/345/6789' or '12 345 6789' and Parish and Holding are empty, when the trader presses Save and continue, then the number is saved as 123456789 and the consignment addresses page shows it as 12/345/6789. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; req-2122)

Given the trader pastes '12/345/6789' into County, with JavaScript on or off, when they press Save and continue, then it is saved as 123456789, the same as typing it, and focus never moved while pasting. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; req-2122)

Given County holds something that is not 9 digits once spaces and slashes are removed, such as '1234', and Parish and Holding are empty, when the trader saves, then today's per-part error messages show and the boxes keep what was typed. (req-715; c-114)
Given the trader enters 12, 345 and 6789 in the three boxes, when they save, then it is saved as 123456789, as today. (req-709)

notes: Approach chosen: drop the maxlength attributes and let the server split a whole number typed or pasted into County, rather than a script that spreads a paste across the boxes. It is the only one of the two that works without JavaScript, it adds no client script to the page, and it covers typing straight through as well as pasting. The 2, 3 and 4 widths still show the number's shape.

Server: when Parish and Holding are empty and County, with spaces and slashes removed, is exactly 9 digits, split it into 2, 3 and 4 before the existing per-part checks. Anything else goes through today's checks unchanged.

Tests: the fit spec asserts maxlength 2, 3 and 4 today (cph-number.fit.spec.js:99-106). Change those asserts to the widths and add the typed-in-one-go and pasted cases, with JavaScript on and off.
